chunk.chapter_title: 66. The Birth of Kusha and Lava
chunk.text:
Having heard the dreadful story of that monarch, Shatrughna, 
paying obeisance to that great Rishi, entered the leaf-thatched 
hut. 
CHAPTER 66 
The Birth of Kusha and Lava 
Now, during the night that Sbatrughna passed in the leaf-
thatched hut, Sita gave birth to two children and, at midnight, 
the youthful ascetics brought the pleasant and auspicious tidings 
to Valmiki, saying :-
" 0 Blessed One, Rams's consort has given birth to twin sons, 
do thou perform the rites that will preserve them from evil 
forces." 
Hearing these words, the great Rishi went to see those newly-
born Ones, who were as effulgent as the new moon and full of 
vignur, like unto twin offspring of the Gods. 
Coming to where Sita was, on beholding those two infants, his 
heart was filled with delight and he performed the Rakshasa 
Rite.' Taking a handful of Kusba Grass with its roots, that 
Twice-born One, Valmiki, pronounced the formula of protection 
for the destruction of evil forces, saying :-
" Since they will rub the first born of the children with the 
Kusba Grass' blessed by the aid of Mantras, his name shall be 
Kusha and, as the last born will be carefully dried by the female 
ascetics with the roots of the grass, he shall be called Lava. 
Therefore those two shall be called Kusba and Lava and, by 
these names that I have given them, they will become renowned." 
Thereafter, the female ascetics purified themselves and 
reverently received the grass from the bands of the Muni, 
applying it to the two children. The rite having been performed 
in the night, Sbatrughna hearing the pleasant tidings, the names 
the children would bear, and Rams's praises, also that Sita bad 
undergone this double and fortunate birth, approached the leaf-
thatched hut where Sita lay and said :-
" 0 Mother, be thou happy!"

brief.summary_1line: In Valmiki’s hermitage, Sita gives birth to twin sons; Valmiki performs protective rites and names them Kusha and Lava.

image_candidates.scene_text: In the quiet hermitage at midnight, Valmiki gazes with joy at Sita’s newborn twins lying beside her on a simple leaf bed.
Valmiki raises sacred kusha grass while chanting mantras over the radiant newborn twins to protect them from evil forces.
Female ascetics gently touch the infants with kusha grass as the sage declares their names, Kusha and Lava, inside the leaf-thatched hut.

deep.rich_summary: During the night that Shatrughna stays at Valmiki’s forest hermitage, Sita gives birth to twin sons. Young ascetics inform the sage Valmiki, who immediately visits the newborns, marveling at their radiance and performing protective rites to ward off evil forces. Using sacred kusa grass and mantras, he conducts a ritual purification and naming ceremony. The first child, touched with consecrated kusa grass, is named Kusha; the second, dried with its roots by the women ascetics, is named Lava. The hermitage community carefully completes the protective rites. When Shatrughna hears the joyful news, he approaches Sita’s hut and offers blessings. This quiet but pivotal moment introduces Kusha and Lava, the future heirs of Rama and the transmitters of the Ramayana itself.

highlight_spans.why: The chapter’s central revelation: the birth of the twins who will carry Rama’s lineage forward.
Marks the moment of Sita giving birth in the forest hermitage, an emotionally significant turning point.
Valmiki begins the ritual explanation connecting sacred kusa grass, mantras, and the naming of the children.
The decisive naming of Lava, completing the identity of the legendary pair Kusha and Lava.
Shatrughna’s tender blessing to Sita captures the quiet emotional warmth surrounding the birth.

top_scenes.scene_text: Inside Valmiki’s forest hermitage at midnight, ascetics gather as Sita lies with her newborn twin sons while the sage prepares sacred kusa grass for a protective ritual.
Valmiki, radiant and solemn, holds a handful of sacred kusa grass over the glowing newborn twins as he chants mantras to name them Kusha and Lava.
Shatrughna stands respectfully at the entrance of Sita’s leaf-thatched hut in the quiet forest night, offering blessings after hearing of the twins’ birth.
